title: The AI Ledger
introduction: An in-progress weekly edition reviewed through November 12. Anthropic adds customer-hosted agent orchestration, while Codex changes Vertex tool streaming. Earlier model and harness reports retain their original dates. The November 11 snapshot is preserved verbatim. Existing November 16–22 forecasts remain unchanged and pending; no new model-launch rumor met the evidence threshold. Confidence is qualitative, not a probability.

items.title: Nov 12: Claude moves the Managed Agents service onto customer infrastructure
items.summary: Anthropic now offers self-hosted Managed Agents: the service, agent loop, sandboxes and session storage run on customer infrastructure. Access requires contacting an Anthropic account team. This is deployment control, not a new model or an offline Claude release.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can retain session state locally and route inference through their chosen provider. Model requests still send conversation content to that provider. Operators take responsibility for securing the server, database and isolated workers; self-hosting does not by itself prevent data leaving the network.
items.confidenceReason: The dated official release entry and linked technical guide agree on scope and access. They do not establish general self-service availability or independently validated security.
items.historicalContext: Earlier self-hosted sandboxes moved only tool execution. This release additionally moves the service and storage. Inference remains separate, and some hosted-service features are unavailable.

items.title: Added Nov 12 · late Nov 11 release: Codex streams Vertex tool updates by default
items.summary: Codex CLI 0.167.2 enables incremental tool updates by default on Google Cloud Vertex AI. The official release says to set incremental_tools_legacy_gcp = false under [features] in config.toml to opt out.
items.whyItMatters: Vertex users should check how their integrations handle streamed tool updates before upgrading. This is a provider-path behavior change, not a new coding model or a measured speed improvement.
items.confidenceReason: The stable GitHub release directly records the behavior and opt-out; its publication timestamp is verified through the GitHub API.
items.historicalContext: Published at 22:44:46 UTC on November 11, after the prior edition’s 20:00 UTC cutoff. Some aggregators label it November 12; this entry retains the original UTC release date.

items.title: Nov 11: Qwen4-Max opens a time-limited API preview
items.summary: Alibaba opened Qwen4-Max-Preview through Token Plan, without pay-as-you-go access. It accepts text, images and video, with a one-million-token context and tool calling. The preview ends at 24:00 November 25 (UTC+8), equivalent to 16:00 UTC that day; this build is then scheduled for retirement.
items.whyItMatters: Plan evaluations around that deadline. In Chat Completions, max_tokens now caps thinking and the final answer together for this model. An answer-only budget can truncate responses; older Qwen models retain their prior behavior.
items.confidenceReason: The dated official changelog verifies preview availability. The documentation establishes access and API behavior, not independent evidence of superior coding performance.
items.historicalContext: The API compatibility notice is dated November 2, before the November 11 preview opening. Neither document establishes a permanent release date or an open-weight Qwen4 release.

items.title: Nov 11: Qwen Code 1.0 previews the combined Qoder harness
items.summary: Qwen Code 1.0 Preview brings together Qoder and Qwen Code agent capabilities. Native packages cover macOS, Linux and Windows without a separate Node.js installation. It supports multiple providers, saved-session resumption and non-interactive runs.
items.whyItMatters: Treat this as a migration to evaluate, not a stable 1.0 upgrade: interfaces, configuration and behavior may change. The tagged README temporarily closes community pull requests and expects them to reopen after December 2026; issues remain welcome.
items.confidenceReason: The official GitHub release is explicitly marked prerelease. Its feature descriptions are publisher claims, not independently tested reliability results.
items.historicalContext: Published November 11 at 03:55 UTC, after stable 0.27.2 on November 10. This harness preview is separate from the Qwen4-Max model preview and does not satisfy a stable-release forecast.

items.title: Added Nov 11 · Nov 10 release: Gemini CLI improves session recovery
items.summary: Stable Gemini CLI 0.68.0 adds an extension-validation command and fixes model selection across transient fallback, cancellation and rewind. ACP session loading now waits for history replay before responding.
items.whyItMatters: Teams using resumed sessions or extensions gain targeted reliability fixes. Concurrent extension installs use a per-extension lock, and shadow repositories honor Git exclude settings. Test these paths in your own setup before relying on the reported fixes.
items.confidenceReason: The official stable release lists the changes. This newsletter has not reproduced the fixes or measured their impact.
items.historicalContext: Published November 10 at 21:17 UTC, after this newsletter’s November 10 cutoff. The 0.68.0 preview appeared November 4; the separate 0.69.0 preview remains a prerelease. This is a harness release, not a new Gemini model.

items.title: Nov 10: Gemini 4 Carbon reaches general availability
items.summary: Google opened Carbon to paid API developers and enterprises, with a rollout to AI Ultra subscribers. Antigravity’s coordinated-agent /swarm feature is in preview; Carbon for cyber retains a separate Fairwind application.
items.whyItMatters: Standard API rates are $2 input/$10 output per million tokens through November 30, rising to $4/$20 on December 1. Output includes thinking; there is no free tier. Budget for the scheduled increase and measured task usage.
items.confidenceReason: The dated API changelog confirms general availability. Performance comparisons and multi-agent demos remain Google’s claims, not tests reproduced here.
items.historicalContext: Carbon was announced October 28 with limited cyber-defender access. November 10 is a broader availability milestone, not the model’s first announcement.

items.title: Nov 10: Copilot CLI adds network-range controls and clearer failures
items.summary: Copilot CLI 1.0.109 adds IPv4/IPv6 CIDR ranges to sandbox host allow/deny rules. Failed prompt-mode JSON runs now emit a final result with an exit status; ACP hooks requesting approval are routed to the client.
items.whyItMatters: Network-scoped deployments gain more precise rules, and scripts get clearer failure records. The notes also add Fable 5.2 to the model picker. That is integration support, not a new model launch.
items.confidenceReason: The official stable release documents these changes. Permission and reliability fixes are publisher-reported and need testing against each team’s configuration.
items.historicalContext: Published November 10 at 17:02 UTC, after the previously covered 1.0.107. Its permission changes satisfy the November 10–15 follow-up forecast published on November 9.

items.title: Nov 10: OpenCode adds Copilot Auto routing and billing fixes
items.summary: OpenCode 2.2.7 lets eligible Copilot accounts select Auto for per-session model routing, with a default-model fallback if routing fails. Session costs now use Copilot’s charged amounts, and cache-warming costs enter totals.
items.whyItMatters: Better accounting can make agent budgets easier to audit. MCP refresh fixes target concurrent token rotations and transient failures. SDK consumers should review breaking changes to image responses and plugin-loading waits before upgrading.
items.confidenceReason: The official stable release verifies announced behavior. It gives no Auto discount percentage or equal-quality savings measurement; no such performance claim is inferred here.
items.historicalContext: Published November 10 at 10:37 UTC, following November 6’s 2.2.6 scripted-session and MCP-pooling update.

items.title: Nov 10 UTC: Hermes fixes silently stale plugin catalogs
items.summary: Hermes Agent 0.23.1 raises its plugin-catalog size cap from 2 MiB to 16 MiB. The live catalog had outgrown the old limit, causing clients to fall back silently to bundled entries and miss newer plugins or removal entries.
items.whyItMatters: The notes say older clients remain affected until updated. Update paths differ: this patch does not change the separately installed .exe/.dmg Desktop app. Do not assume a CLI or container update updates every surface.
items.confidenceReason: Official stable release notes describe the failure and fix; the behavior has not been independently reproduced here.
items.historicalContext: The notes label the release November 9, while GitHub published it November 10 at 01:42 UTC. This edition uses the latter and preserves both dates. Curated notes for its broader bundled changes are deferred to 0.24.0.

items.confidenceReason: The official stable release directly states the integration and fallback behavior.

items.title: Added Nov 10 · Nov 9 launch: Muse Ember targets repeated agent work
items.summary: Meta released Muse Ember on its Model API and Muse Code plans for tasks such as tool calls, coding subtasks and document processing. It accepts text, images, audio and video.
items.whyItMatters: Input/output rates are $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens for prompts up to 200K input tokens, and $0.30/$1.50 above that threshold. Long context does not carry the headline low rate across every workload.
items.confidenceReason: Official research and developer posts establish availability and the pricing tiers. Vendor-presented comparisons are not independent validation of universal superiority.
items.historicalContext: This is a November 9 release added one day later. Meta positions Ember as a smaller execution worker paired with larger planning models, rather than a replacement for every reasoning task.

items.confidenceReason: The announcement verifies availability and pricing. Claimed capability and speed gains are vendor results, not independent replication.
items.historicalContext: This November 9 release follows 5.1. It does not explicitly resolve the older user-intent rumor preserved in the prior edition.

items.title: Nov 9: Claude Code adds Fable 5.2 and security fixes
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.321 makes Fable 5.2 the default Fable model. Release notes report fixes for MCP OAuth secrets following cross-host redirects and several Bash permission and sandbox checks.
items.whyItMatters: Review this upgrade for agent environments using MCP credentials or shell tools. Remote Control also gains a settings-file option that stops new sessions if the file changes until restart.
items.confidenceReason: The stable release is official. Security fixes remain publisher claims, not proof of complete protection.
items.historicalContext: Released November 9 at 19:22 UTC, following 2.1.319 on November 6. This satisfies the documented-control-update forecast published November 8.
